artworks.title: Spoliarium
artworks.description: Gift of Spain to the Philippines; National Fine Arts Collection; National Cultural Treasure; Photo by Bengy Toda IIIThe Spoliarium is Juan Luna’s most enormous artwork in the Philippines. This monumental work of art won the gold medal during the 1884 Madrid Exposition of Fine Arts.

artworks.title: El asesinato del Gobernador Bustamante (The Assassination of Governor Bustamante), also known as La Iglesia contra el estado (The Church against the State)
artworks.description: Circa 1904; The Gift of Cecilia Yulo-Locsin in memory of Leandro V. Locsin; National Fine Arts Collection; National Cultural Treasure; Photo by Bengy Toda IIIThis painting is Hidalgo’s interpretation of a violent and historical event involving Fernando Bustamante and the Spanish friars in Manila during the Spanish colonial period.

artworks.title: Filipino Struggles Through History
artworks.description: Collection of the Government of the City of Manila; On loan to the National Museum of the Philippines courtesy of Mayor Francisco Moreno Domagoso and the Manila City Council; National Cultural TreasureThis painting was commissioned by Mayor Antonio Villegas for the Manila City Hall in 1968 and told of the saga of the Filipino people through the centuries.

artworks.title: The International Rice Research Institute (IRRI) Series
artworks.description: On loan from the collection of the International Rice Research Institute (IRRI); National Cultural Treasure; Photo by Bengy Toda IIIThese large-scale paintings completed in 1962, tell of the rural life and the spectacle of small-town activities of the Filipinos, particularly in Los Baños, Laguna, where IRRI is situated.

artworks.title: Una Bulaqueña
artworks.description: National Fine Arts Collection; National Cultural Treasure; Photo by Bengy Toda IIIUna Bulaquena, or The Woman from Bulacan, is one of Luna’s paintings he did when he returned to the Philippines in 1894. Luna’s expertise and excellence in the traditional style are manifested in this painting with her lifelike rendition of the details of the Bulaqueña’s piña.

artworks.title: Interieure d’un Café (Parisian Life)
artworks.description: On loan from the collection of the Government Service Insurance System; National Cultural TreasureThis painting captures Dr. Jose Rizal, Dr. Ariston Bautista, and Juan Luna sitting and having a relaxed time in a café in Paris, France.

artworks.title: Alimentando a las gallinas (Feeding the Chickens)
artworks.artist: Simón Flores y de la Rosa
artworks.description: National Fine Arts Collection; National Cultural Treasure; Photo by Bengy Toda IIIThis outstanding painting is considered to be one of the few extant genre paintings of the artist, having painted mostly religious art and portraits in his lifetime

artworks.title: Progress of Medicine in the Philippines
artworks.description: Panel I of IV; On loan from the collection of the Philippine General Hospital; National Cultural Treasure; Photo by Bengy Toda IIIThis painting completed in 1953 is composed of four parts. It depicted the evolution of healing practices in the Philippines from the pre-colonial period to the modern period .

artworks.title: Calesa
artworks.description: National Fine Arts Collection; Photo by Bengy Toda IIIVicente Manansala was one of the notable modernists in the country. He developed a unique style called transparent cubism wherein the figures still appear recognizable amidst the colorful geometric patterns. He also expanded his subject matter to postwar urban realities depicting the struggles of displacement and poverty. This style is present in his work Calesa (1951).

artworks.title: Belleza Filipina (Filipina Beauty)
artworks.description: Circa 1920; National Fine Arts Collection; Photo by Bengy Toda III Jorge Pineda was a notable illustrator for Renacimiento, a Filipino weekly magazine, and Claro M. Recto’s “Bajo los cocoteros”. His pastel drawing Belleza Filipina/Filipina Beauty (circa 1920) depicts a lady with a handful of paint tubes symbolizing the role of women as culture bearers.

artworks.title: Bodegon
artworks.description: National Fine Arts Collection; Photo by Bengy Toda IIICreated in 1912 when Celedonia Domingo Ongpin was only 16 years old, this Bodegon (Still Life) pastel drawing is an example of the popular subject matter during the American colonial period. During that time, works depicting landscapes, portraits, and still life served as souvenirs for visitors and art patrons.

artworks.title: Untitled (Sketches)
artworks.description: Undated; National Fine Arts Collection; Photo by Bengy Toda IIIThis graphite sketch of a lady by National Artist Fernando Amorsolo is one of his many sketches from the National Fine Arts Collection. Although rough and unfinished, this sketch represents Amorsolo’s exceptional skill in figurative art.

artworks.title: Lost in the Forest
artworks.description: Undated; National Fine Arts Collection; Photo by Bengy Toda IIIAn important modernist painter, Carlos “Botong” Francisco’s Lost in the Forest represents his unique subject matter depicting indigenous colors and themes such as local history and mythology. This style is also apparent in many of his murals and large-scale paintings.

artworks.title: Cariñosa
artworks.description: National Fine Arts Collection; Photo by Bengy Toda IIICariñosa (1962) represented one of Manuel Rodriguez Sr.’s early works in the 1960s when he was exploring lithography with fellow printmakers and founded the Philippine Association of Printmakers (PAP) in 1968. He popularized genre subjects with folk quality in many of his prints, such as this one.

artworks.title: Utang Panlabas (A/P)
artworks.description: Gift of Leonilo Doloricon; National Fine Arts Collection; Photo by Bengy Toda IIILeonilo Doloricon was part of the Social Realist, a group of artists who aims to present the socio-political conditions of the country. In his work Utang Panlabas (2014), Doloricon presents the financial struggles of the country using symbolisms such as the Philippine flag, death skeleton, IMF for International Monetary Fund, WB for World Bank, and tubo, meaning interest.

artworks.title: Untitled II
artworks.description: National Fine Arts Collection; Photo by Bengy Toda IIIUntitled II (1969) was one of Ofelia Gelvezon Tequi’s early works after returning to the country from her Special Studies in Graphic Arts at the Pratt Institute in 1968. This print shows embossed shapes on paper, and this printmaking process also imitates plate marks in lithographs or screenprints.

artworks.title: Improvisation Mindanao 4/10
artworks.description: National Fine Arts Collection; Photo by Bengy Toda IIIBrenda Fajardo is one of the female artists who convey feminist themes in her works. In her Improvisation Mindanao 4/10 (1969), Fajardo features women and their struggles amidst the Moro insurgency in the Mindanao region that started in 1968.

artworks.title: Mga Ninuno VIII
artworks.description: National Fine Arts Collection; Photo by Bengy Toda IIIImelda Cajipe Endaya was one of the printmakers who focuses on themes about national identity. In her Mga Ninuno VIII (1979), she depicts two types of figures: black and white figures in pre-colonial attire and smudged figures in Spanish colonial attire. In the background is an image of Doctrina Christiana, an early book on Catholicism.

artworks.title: Dreamers Zone II
artworks.description: National Fine Arts Collection; Photo by Bengy Toda IIIDreamers Zone II (1979) is one of the early works of Impy Pilapil as a printmaker consisting mainly of serigraphs and lithographs. Fresh from her studies at the Pratt Graphic Institute in New York, she later joined the Printmakers Association of the Philippines (PAP). Her works are mainly influenced by anthroposophy, a spiritual path to a better understanding of the physical world leading to insight into the spiritual world.

artworks.title: Untitled (C.T.P. I)
artworks.description: National Fine Arts Collection; Photo by Bengy Todaa IIIIleana Lee is a conceptual artist who later joined the Printmakers Association of the Philippines (PAP). She combined the philosophies of conceptual art in graphic arts resulting in her experimental abstract prints, as seen in her work C.T.P. I (1980).

artworks.title: The Silent One
artworks.description: National Fine Arts Collection; Photo by Bengy Toda IIIBenedicto Cabrera was one of the artists in the 1970s who seek to portray the Filipino identity. The Silent One (1979) represents this theme using images of a mother and an older woman. May relate Cabrera’s use of women images to his symbolism in his Sabel series, symbolizing the woman, Filipinas, as a victim of exploitation.

artworks.title: Mount Pulag Facing Baguio
artworks.medium: Durst Lambda print on Fujiflex paper
artworks.description: The Gift of Bengy Toda III; National Fine Arts CollectionMount Pulag is the third highest mountain in the Philippines and the highest peak in Luzon. This photograph, taken in 2015 shows the breathtaking scenery of the mountain popular among hikers and nature lovers.

artworks.title: Ingredients of Palapa
artworks.medium: National Fine Arts CollectionThis photograph is part of the exhibition, Pagkaing Filipino: Images of Regional Cuisine Dishes, Drinks, and Delicacies and their stories by Neal Oshima, currently exhibited at the Ilocos Regional Museum. Palapa is a popular spicy side dish in Maranao cuisine. This condiment is made of sakurab, a type of shallot, ginger, coconut, onions, garlic, chilli, and salt.
artworks.description: Marawi City, Lanao del Sur; The Gift of Neal Oshima

artworks.title: Portrait of Serapia N. Santos y Aduna (1881-1929)
artworks.description: Foto-óleo on board; National Fine Arts CollectionThis foto-óleo was done by Ramon Peralta, a leading scenographer and mentor to artist, Vicente Manansala. Peralta painted this foto-óleo portrait three years after Serapia’s death and served as her family’s memento mori, a posthumous remembrance of her.

artworks.title: Portrait of Anita Concepcion Meñez Ramos (1913-1957)
artworks.description: Circa early 1950s; The Gift of the Godofredo P. Ramos Foundation, Inc.; National Fine Arts CollectionAnita Conception Meñez Ramos was married to Congressman Godofredo P. Ramos of Aklan. This foto-óleo was created around 1951 to 1953 on a black and white photograph of Anita and Godofredo. Anita is wearing a terno which we presume was from hand-colored piña fabric woven by the women of Aklan.

artworks.title: Mother and Son
artworks.artist: Jake Lagonera (Photographer) and Mario de Rivera (Painter)
artworks.medium: Acrylic on natural white matte canvas
artworks.description: The Gift of the Artists; National Fine Arts CollectionMother and Son was part of the exhibition When Lens Meets Brush launched in 2016 at the National Museum of Anthropology. Referred to as “paintographs,” photographer Jake Lagonera collaborated with painter Mario di Rivera in this 2016 photo which was among those donated by the Leica Club Manila to the NMP.

artworks.title: Anita Magsaysay-Ho b. 1914, Manila – d. 2012
artworks.description: Painter; The Gift of Isa Lorenzo; National Fine Arts Collection“I know very well the strength, hard work and quiet dignity of Philippine women, for after all, I am one of them.” Magsaysay-Ho is regarded as one of the country’s pioneering modernist painters. She is the lone female artist in National Artist Victorio Edades’ list of the “Thirteen Moderns”.

artworks.title: Kaamulan Festival of Bukidnon
artworks.description: Photograph on sintra board; The Gift of George Tapan; National Fine Arts CollectionThe Kamulan Festival honors and celebrates the customs and traditions of the seven ethnolinguistic groups in the region namely: Bukidnon, Higaonon, Talaandig, Manobo, Matigsalug, Tigwahanon, and Umayamnon. Award-winning photographer George Tapan took this particular photo in 2015 and was donated as part of the National Fine Arts Collection that same year.

artworks.title: Caricature of President Elpidio Quirino
artworks.description: Undated; National Fine Arts Collection; Photo by Bengy Toda IIIThis watercolor caricature portrays President Elpidio Quirino using sweeping strokes, creating an abstract image of the former president.

artworks.title: This Man is Dying
artworks.description: National Fine Arts Collection; Photo by Bengy Toda IIIA prominent political cartoonist of his time, Pereira was a member of the editorial staff and eventually the Philippine Free Press chief artist.
